newsitem.title: USA: Judge refuses to delay start of Fla. tobacco suit.
newsitem.headline: Judge refuses to delay start of Fla. tobacco suit.

text.p: A Florida judge on Friday rejected a tobacco industry request that the August 4 start of a high stakes suit by the state government be delayed.

The tobacco industry had asked that the Florida state government suit seeking to recoup costs for treating sick smokers through its Medicaid program be delayed until a class action suit to be tried in September in Miami is concluded.
The Miami trial scheduled to begin in September is on behalf of all ill Florida smokers and their survivors.
Lawyers for Philip Morris Co Inc and other tobacco companies argued that many of the issues in the trial would be identical and that simultaneous trials would be redundant.
Lawyers representing the State of Florida dismissed the request, calling it a delaying tactic by the tobacco industry.
"I am going to deny the motion to stay," Palm Beach County Circuit Court Judge Harold Cohen said during a hearing.
He said the Florida state lawsuit was distinguished from the class action suit because it was being brought under a special law passed by the Florida legislature in 1994.
